links.outcome: Jailbreak attack success rate of LLMs on Chinese medical ethics themes
links.effect: Jailbreak ASR reached 82.1%, an ASR Gain of over 80 percentage points; five models including Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-4.1 had ASRs of 96% to 100%; Claude-Sonnet-4-Reasoning was most robust.
links.quote: A systemic collapse of defenses was observed, whereas models demonstrated high baseline compliance, the jailbreak ASR reached 82.1%, representing an ASR Gain of over 80 percentage points.

links.outcome: Maintenance of safety boundaries under adversarial multi-turn role-play prompting
links.effect: Under role-playing, scenario simulation and multi-turn dialogue, jailbreak ASR reached 82.1% (ASR Gain over 80 points), with five models at 96-100% ASR despite high baseline compliance.
links.quote: A systemic collapse of defenses was observed, whereas models demonstrated high baseline compliance, the jailbreak ASR reached 82.1%, representing an ASR Gain of over 80 percentage points.

unlisted_practices: Transition from outcome supervision to process supervision of LLM outputs
Multi-factor identity verification for users of LLMs

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the susceptibility of various LLMs to adversarial jailbreak prompts concerning medical ethics violations, but evaluates baseline model robustness without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
